An Account of the Human Good Into Life Perspectives Essay

Introduction

In the first section of the reading provided, various matters determine the human good. According to the book, one can be happy depending on the decisions made and actions taken regarding the choice made about an issue. For example, if one builds a house, they will feel happy, and if they also feel healthy, the aspect of good is also revealed. In other words, the writer is trying to help the reader navigate that the human good can be achieved under everything as long as the subject is affiliated with the person behind it. Human beings choose some of the factors to define their happiness and aspect of goodness (Aristotle 8). Most people choose general instruments of life such as wealth, flutes, and many others.

Assessment of Important Issues, Themes, and Concerns of the Readings

Complete good is determined by self-sufficiency, which means a person will live according to the estimated limit when dealing with matters. The aspect of human good can be extended from one party to another, such as from parents to their children or friends to friends (Aristotle 8). According to the inner picture portrayed by the book, it seems human beings are structured in political, social, and economic settings that come in different formulas for achieving the common good. Happiness can be an agreeable subject, measured by what people feel concerning the completeness of human anatomy and general ways of living. Some elements such as the interdependence that people have with the environment can be associated with human good. Therefore, what is spoken or conveyed during sensitive societal settings defines the completeness of human beings (Aristotle 9). For example, if one is educated and has the roots of success, it means that the people who have been backing the person may benefit from the same, hence building the goodness more.

The sketch of good can be drawn by showing what one has and what one lacks. The degree to which people seem to be satisfied by normal happenings such as rainfall, weather changes, and relationships with others can be a measure of good (Aristotle 9). A carpenter example is given to show the extent of discipline they have when it comes to measurements. In this matter, people have to do what appears more logical even if it may not be what they wish. These factors will be a limit to human beings, and they show the restrictions that are important in life.

Some questions may arise from this context, and the reader may be baffled by the issues discussed in the book. First, how possible is it for human beings to be good to everyone if every aspect of the common good is self-centered? Second, can all people be the same in terms of traits that make them happy? And if they must be happy and do human good, what about the deficits left more so the environment such as plants, pets, and world animals? Thus, interrogating such issues in one’s mind may help one understand the account of human good and life perspectives.

Critical Analysis of the Text

The author has given a defense of the account of the good by supporting it with various elements. The main idea here is that the conclusions that people make from given premises will be harmonized by the true accounts of the subject matter (Aristotle 10). The truth must be compromised with false, and therefore, the clash between the two variables is seen in terms of the reaction and outcome of the matter. To understand the human good that the writer is talking about, people must think about the external, bodily, and soul perspectives. These three elements may notably categorize the metrics that can define the accounts of good in human life (Aristotle 10). The soul is often considered to offer a full account of the good from what people reason and decide to do with their reasoning.

The author means that the soul is more powerful than the body in that the cognition of the account or the outcome of a task is articulated from the soul. It is important not to overlook the body as the doer. The context brought to light is that accounts of human goods are structured and reasoned by the soul before getting to the external perspectives. Happiness is a form of justifying the accounts of human good since many consider it a virtue (Aristotle 12). For example, if one is asleep or ill, they may not be feeling happy about it as some consider sleeping a measure of laxity while others say that illness is brought by evil. In short, human beings must engage in societal frameworks that define the ways of living, and the cultural essence is felt significantly at this point.

Active people always feel happy about the level of engagement they have daily. For example, a person working in a busy food outlet may feel pleased by the nature of their job for various reasons. First, it enables them not to see a long day and keeps them focused and developing their minds and souls. Second, the personal interactions with the guests during food and beverage service may make them learn various aspects of life (Aristotle 12). Hence, they may feel like they have a significant role in teaching others the same. These factors make people happy, and they are considered the root sources of human good.

Happiness is achieved in various ways, according to the text. By reading the topic well, indeed, one may not be able to differentiate whether happiness is achieved by learning or habituation (Aristotle 12). To elaborate on this matter, it is more reasonable to say that it is cultivated from both. Here, a reader has to understand a critical point on this note. First, creating own happiness is a way learned from life exploration. Second, habits that one has grown with may be a determining factor in achieving happiness. For example, if one knew that going to church is one way of becoming morally stable in society, then such people may be active in religion as they feel it strengthens their human good. By this point, it will be true to say that they have achieved happiness from habituation.

Though, by keenly reading the book, one may wonder why happiness was not given as the super element of human good, assuming that it is a gift from God (Aristotle 11). This question probes one to investigate the possibility of having achievements that may not make one happy. The other concern from the topic is the level of happiness that one has to achieve, given that it can be a matter of self-efficacy and sociological well-being. The issue of fortune is a contentious matter at twilight since the book may not unveil the natural state of fineness that can be entrusted to bring human good.

While reading the topic, it is clear that happiness is an activity of the soul, as mentioned earlier in this essay. Some goods determine the necessary conditions for happiness. The writer means that if one is healthy, wealthy, or successful, one can be triggered by the inner spirit from the soul to feel happy (Aristotle 14). These accounts of goods in human anatomy make it possible to achieve happiness. The political setting in the current society makes people express their happiness, and therefore, the metrics involved may be as forms of human goods. For example, diplomatic tensions probe people to start analyzing the power a given country has over the other. This, people, become happy when they notice their side is winning while the other party is losing.

Similarly, a successful person may not be prosperous in matters in life, and that at some point, levels the human way of living hence, creating ways for people to experience good. If one had a breakthrough almost in whatever undertaking they came across, but they fail in the end, no one can say they die while happy (Aristotle 14). Therefore, the author means that happiness must be simultaneous with life aspects driven by cultural and ethical cues.

There is concern about whether a human being may be happy during their lifetime through the book. For a reader to understand this, they must think about whether it is possible for one to be happy every time. According to the facts of life, the dead knows nothing, and therefore, they cannot feel happy when they do not live anymore. That brings the focus on whether or not human beings can be happy during their lifetime. It is important to consider the matters that make one happy and the duration in which the issues last to answer the question. For example, if one lived in blessings that made their life to be bright, it means at that point they were happy, and they had been satisfied by the human good.

However, these kinds of people may at one point suffer from misfortune or unfortunate event that distorts their happiness significantly. From the understanding of the chapter, it is normal to experience both evil and good when one is living (Aristotle 15). Therefore, human beings can never be happy all their lifetime due to the uncertainties that come from time to time. However, a significant portion of human life is characterized by happiness from the human good (Aristotle 16). Even when someone is poor, they have many elements that make them happy as long as they feel contented with the little owned. Therefore, human goods that define happiness must balance the period in which one lives to determine if one can live happily or not.

Conclusion

The above text has given a rationale for human accounts of good when it comes to life. The book has given strong points about human good such as the decisions and actions that are taken to determine happiness. Additionally, human good is influenced by people’s perceptions concerning various events in life. The gap that has been left and needs to be researched is the relationship between human good and social well-being. Does it mean that it is difficult to have everyone happy and satisfied in their life? And if it is hard to please everyone, what measure of human good or the level of the subject can neutralize life situations so that everyone is happy? From researching the above elements, it will be easy to establish human good that drives people towards happiness and breakthrough in life.

Cryptocurrency has become a widely debated topic over the last decade, attracting both fervent supporters and harsh critics. While some people argue that digital currencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum represent the future of money, others see them as nothing more than speculative bubbles destined to burst. This essay aims to explore both sides of this argument and provide a balanced view on whether cryptocurrency truly holds promise as a new financial system or whether it is an unstable market driven mainly by speculation.

The concept of cryptocurrency was introduced to offer a decentralized, secure, and efficient means of conducting financial transactions without the need for traditional banks. Digital currencies rely on blockchain technology, which records transactions transparently and immutably. Proponents argue that cryptocurrencies could reduce transaction fees, increase financial inclusion for people without bank accounts, and even provide a hedge against inflation in countries with unstable currencies. For instance, El Salvador’s recent adoption of Bitcoin as legal tender was aimed at fostering financial inclusion and attracting investment, highlighting practical applications of cryptocurrencies beyond speculation.

However, the volatility of cryptocurrencies raises serious concerns about their reliability as a store of value or as a practical medium of exchange. Prices can swing wildly within a short time, making them risky for everyday use. Bitcoin, for example, experienced a dramatic rise to nearly $65,000 in April 2021 before dropping below $30,000 months later. Such fluctuations demonstrate that many investors may be attracted by the potential for huge profits rather than the underlying utility of the asset. Therefore, it is hard to distinguish whether cryptocurrencies are truly changing the concept of money or if they simply represent a highly speculative investment.

Moreover, the lack of regulation in many countries creates an uncertain environment for cryptocurrencies. While decentralization is one of the core benefits celebrated by its supporters, it also means there is little legal protection for users and investors. Scams, hacks, and fraud have been common in the crypto market, leading to significant losses for many individuals. The collapse of the Mt. Gox exchange in 2014, where hundreds of millions of dollars worth of Bitcoins were stolen, is an example that shaken public confidence. Consequently, governments and financial institutions remain cautious or even hostile towards cryptocurrencies, limiting their widespread adoption.

On the other hand, technological advancements continue to improve the crypto ecosystem. Newer cryptocurrencies and blockchain projects aim to solve some of the problems linked with early digital currencies, including scalability, transaction speed, and energy consumption. Ethereum’s shift towards proof-of-stake consensus is designed to be more energy-efficient, addressing environmental criticisms frequently levied against Bitcoin. These developments suggest that the cryptocurrency market is evolving and could become more practical and sustainable over time, potentially transforming the way we think about money.

Nonetheless, the current speculative nature of many cryptocurrencies cannot be ignored. Meme coins like Dogecoin have seen massive price surges driven mostly by social media hype and celebrity endorsements rather than fundamental value. Such trends resemble past financial bubbles, such as the dot-com bubble in the late 1990s, where irrational enthusiasm led to overvaluation followed by a market crash. Thus, it is important to question whether the enthusiasm behind cryptocurrencies is based on genuine prospects or speculative fervor.

Cryptocurrency undoubtedly poses both exciting opportunities and serious challenges. It is not just one thing—it is many things, depending on the perspective and the specific digital asset considered. While some projects aim to build robust financial tools for the future, others may simply exploit fad-driven investment behavior. The reality is complex, and the outcome uncertain.

In conclusion, cryptocurrency could be the future of money, but the path to this future is fraught with risks and uncertainties. Some digital currencies might find lasting use as payment methods or stores of value, while others may fade away after speculative bubbles burst. For now, it seems wise to approach cryptocurrencies with cautious optimism, recognizing both their potential and their pitfalls. Only time will truly reveal if they will redefine money or just become a passing financial phenomenon.

Universal Basic Income: Solution or Problem?

In recent years, the concept of Universal Basic Income (UBI) has gained significant attention in both academic circles and public debates. At its core, UBI is a regular, unconditional payment given to all citizens regardless of their employment status or income level. This idea aims to provide a minimum financial foundation for everyone, ensuring a basic level of living standard. However, opinions about UBI diverge sharply. While some hail it as a progressive solution to poverty and unemployment, others argue it could create more problems than it solves. Therefore, it is crucial to examine carefully whether Universal Basic Income is truly a solution to societal challenges or if it introduces new complications.

One of the primary arguments in favor of UBI is its potential to reduce poverty and income inequality. Poverty remains a serious issue worldwide, with many people struggling to meet their basic needs. By providing a guaranteed income, UBI could help lift individuals and families out of poverty, enabling them to cover essentials such as food, housing, and healthcare. For example, in Finland, a two-year UBI experiment provided unemployed individuals with a monthly stipend without conditions. The results showed improvement in recipients’ well-being and mental health, indicating that UBI might offer substantial social benefits. Therefore, many see UBI as a straightforward method to enhance social justice.

Moreover, UBI could simplify welfare systems, which are often complex and bureaucratic. Current social support programs typically involve many rules and conditions, such as job searches or income tests. These requirements can discourage people from seeking help or make the process stressful and demeaning. With UBI, the unconditional nature of the payment would eliminate the need for such checks, reducing administrative costs and making social welfare more accessible. Consequently, this could lead to more efficient government spending and reduce the stigma associated with receiving assistance.

Another advantage is that UBI might encourage entrepreneurship and creativity. Many people refrain from pursuing new business ideas or artistic projects because of financial risk. If they had a guaranteed basic income, they might feel more secure to take risks and innovate. This could have positive effects on economic growth and technological advancement. For instance, in places where individuals have safety nets, there tends to be higher rates of startup creation. Therefore, UBI could foster a more dynamic and creative society.

However, despite these positive points, there are substantial concerns about the feasibility and consequences of UBI. Foremost among these is the cost. Providing every citizen with a regular payment would require enormous public expenditure. Critics argue that governments might not be able to afford such programs without raising taxes significantly or cutting other important services. This could burden the economy and the taxpayers. For example, estimates in the United States suggest that a meaningful UBI program could cost trillions of dollars annually. Thus, the financial sustainability of UBI is questionable.

Furthermore, some fear that UBI could reduce the incentive to work. If people receive money regardless of employment, they might choose not to seek jobs or work fewer hours, leading to lower productivity and economic decline. This concern is especially important because work is not only about income but also about purpose and social engagement. Although some studies indicate that the work disincentive might be limited, the long-term cultural effects are uncertain. Therefore, UBI might unintentionally harm labor markets and social cohesion.

In addition, UBI could create inflationary pressures. If everyone suddenly has more money to spend, demand for goods and services might rise faster than supply, leading to higher prices. Inflation can erode the value of the basic income, particularly hurting those it aims to help. This effect might be especially pronounced in housing and essential goods markets. As a result, the real benefit of UBI might be reduced over time, questioning its effectiveness in improving living standards.

Moreover, some critics point out that UBI does not address the root causes of poverty and inequality. It provides money but does not guarantee access to education, healthcare, or meaningful employment. Without these structural changes, people might still face barriers that prevent social mobility. Thus, UBI might be a superficial remedy rather than a deep solution. Therefore, focusing on comprehensive social policies might be more effective than distributing cash alone.

Another downside is the risk of unfairness. While UBI is universal, meaning everyone receives it, this universality might be seen as inefficient. Wealthy individuals who do not need additional income would also receive payments, which many view as a misuse of public funds. More targeted welfare programs concentrate resources on those in genuine need. Therefore, critics argue that UBI could lead to wastefulness and public dissatisfaction.

Despite these concerns, some middle ground solutions have emerged, such as partial basic income or negative income tax systems. These approaches aim to provide financial support but in a more targeted or conditional way, which might reduce costs and disincentives. For example, Alaska’s Permanent Fund distributes oil revenue to residents annually, providing a form of basic income with manageable fiscal impact. Thus, variants of UBI might balance benefits and drawbacks better than a universal unconditional payment.

Moreover, technological changes and automation increase the challenges of future employment. Many jobs are at risk of being replaced by machines, which could lead to higher unemployment and income insecurity. In this context, UBI might become necessary to support people as the economy transforms. It could provide a safety net during transitions and reduce social unrest. Therefore, debates about UBI are closely linked to broader economic and technological trends.

In conclusion, Universal Basic Income is a complex and multi-faceted idea that holds both promise and risk. It could provide a simple and effective way to reduce poverty, promote freedom, and simplify welfare. However, it also faces serious challenges including high costs, potential work disincentives, inflation, and questions about fairness. Therefore, whether UBI is a solution or a problem depends largely on how it is designed and implemented, as well as the specific social context. Policymakers must weigh these factors carefully, considering experiments and evidence before adopting UBI as a wide-scale policy.

Ultimately, Universal Basic Income should not be seen as a one-size-fits-all solution. It is one possible tool among many to address inequality and economic insecurity. While it might work well in some countries or regions, in others it may create unintended difficulties. Therefore, a cautious and balanced approach is needed, combining UBI with other reforms in education, healthcare, and labor markets. By doing so, societies can better ensure that economic progress benefits all citizens equally and sustainably.

In this way, UBI challenges traditional views about work, welfare, and citizenship. It forces us to reconsider what society owes to its members and how to distribute resources fairly. While controversy will likely continue, the discussion is valuable and necessary. It invites innovation in social policy and encourages us to imagine a future where economic security is available to everyone. Therefore, the debate about UBI is not only about economics but about the kind of society we want to live in.

Thus, further research and pilot programs should be encouraged to gather more data on UBI’s effects. Lessons from experiments like those in Finland, Canada, and Kenya provide useful insights but are not definitive. Each country must assess its own needs, values, and capabilities. Therefore, the introduction of UBI should proceed with care, transparency, and ongoing evaluation.

Finally, citizens’ voices must be part of the conversation. Public support or opposition can shape policy success. Understanding how people perceive UBI, their fears and hopes, is essential for designing effective programs. Therefore, open dialogue and education are key components in the future of Universal Basic Income.

Overall, Universal Basic Income remains an intriguing yet controversial idea. It holds potential but also poses risks. The challenge lies in finding a path that maximizes benefits while minimizing harm. Only then can UBI move from a theoretical concept to a practical solution that improves lives.

Nuclear energy has often been a controversial topic, but when it comes to fighting climate change, its role cannot be ignored. The world needs cleaner energy sources to reduce carbon emissions drastically, and nuclear power offers an alternative with low greenhouse gas output. While there are concerns about safety and waste, nuclear energy might be one of the few realistic options to meet the growing energy demand without worsening global warming.

One of the main benefits of nuclear power is its ability to generate large amounts of electricity with very little carbon dioxide released. Unlike fossil fuels, nuclear plants do not emit greenhouse gases during operation. For example, France gets about 70% of its electricity from nuclear power, which helps keep its carbon emissions per capita much lower than countries dependent on coal or natural gas. This shows that nuclear energy can contribute to a cleaner energy mix.

However, critics argue that nuclear energy is risky because of accidents and the challenge of radioactive waste disposal. Events like the Fukushima disaster in 2011 remind people of the potential dangers. Still, advancements in technology have made modern reactors safer and more efficient. Besides, the issue of waste management is being addressed with new methods like deep geological storage, which aims to isolate waste far from the environment.

On the other hand, renewable energy sources such as wind and solar are also important in reducing emissions. Yet, their reliability is affected by weather and time of day, which means nuclear energy can complement these technologies by providing a steady power supply. Without reliable baseload power like nuclear, the electricity grid might struggle to support societies shifting away from fossil fuels.

Furthermore, developing nuclear energy often requires high initial investments and long construction times, which some argue slow down immediate climate action. Nonetheless, once operational, nuclear plants last for decades and produce electricity at a relatively low cost. China’s increasing nuclear capacity demonstrates how investment in nuclear infrastructure can be part of long-term climate strategies.

In conclusion, nuclear energy presents both challenges and opportunities in the fight against climate change. It is not a perfect solution, but its ability to provide large-scale, low-carbon power is important. If safety and waste concerns continue to improve, nuclear power could play a key role in a sustainable energy future.

A Feminist Approach in the Film “Thelma and Louise” Essay

There are extremely few films that explore not only female friendships but also delve into the interpersonal connection of women, seeking to escape the restrictions of gender, class, time, and place. In turn, Scott’s road movie reveals the female nature from the inside. Thelma, married at 18 and tolerating her tyrannical husband, is not as downtrodden and tame as many would like to see. Thelma does not agree to condone, so she packs her things, throws suitcases into her friend’s car, leaves a note for her husband, and goes off with Louise for the whole weekend. If Thelma is an amateur adventurer, then Louise is a serious rebel. Her boyfriend Jimmy has no power over her, but rather she dictates the rules to him, although she is forced to endure his constant adventures while she works as a waitress. Louise does not hesitate to shoot the man who tried to rape her girlfriend.

Seeing the world through the eyes of liberated women driving merrily into the unknown was an innovation that boldly granted a woman the right to be human. Cooper notes that this is a movie about women who defy eternity and openly neglect social conditions. It has a philosophical background in the immortality of the soul and the lofty value of freedom, which despises even death. The film’s finale proves that suicide is preferable to prison, just as lethal injection is better than life imprisonment.

It is a pity that they do not make strong films about women’s struggles in Hollywood anymore; that is why it remains to revise Thelma and Louise from year to year. The current films about women ending with a wedding, and receiving a ring from a man are equated to the moment of personal transformation and self-identification of a woman who is looking for only worldly peace in life. These stereotypical films are forgotten and will never become a symbol of the female spirit, which Thelma and Louise became precisely because it reflects the true woman’s need for freedom.

Smith, in her speech, focuses on gender inequality in cinema. As confirmation, the speaker presents depressing statistics. First, according to Smith, less than a third of all speaking characters are women (2:39). The most unexpected thing is that the situation has not changed for 70 years. As my example, I can cite the world-famous film The Lord of the Rings, where all ten central roles are male. Thus, the woman is still noticeably absent from the screen.

Second, Smith asserts that in addition to gender inequality, Hollywood films are characterized by racial and ethnic discrimination. It is noteworthy that it is possible to expect changes in this direction. In 2020, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced the introduction of special rules that should eliminate inequalities within the organization itself and the film industry. Rottenberg affirms that starting in 2024, films that qualify for the Best Film award must meet at least two of the four criteria. Among them is the presence of actors from an ethnic or racial minority, 30% of the composition of a woman, representatives of the LGBTQ+ community, a racial or ethnic minority, and people with disabilities. Moreover, there must be the same diversity in the production and marketing teams that work on the film, and the film must represent one of the listed minorities. Nevertheless, women remain in the minority since the requirement is 30%, but women are about half of society.

Third, Smith notes that only 4.1% of directors are women (6:00). Moreover, only three of the 886 directors are African American or black, and only one woman is Asian (Smith 6:13). At the same time, there is a pattern between the gender of the director and the peculiarity of the roles in this movie. Thus, the more women participate in creating a movie, the more women appear on the screen, and vice versa. This fact is one of the reasons for the disappointing statistics on the number of women in cinema and the peculiarity of their representation. Therefore, given the disheartening statistics and trends that have taken place in recent years, Hollywood cinema is not a very good place for women.

Chelsey, thanks for your opinion. Indeed, in addition to the motif of freedom and independence, Thelma and Louise unfold with a feminist approach, making women as strong as men. The film’s female perspectives undermine and appropriate the dominant male gaze typical of mainstream Hollywood cinema, using mockery as a narrative device to illustrate the sexism inherent in the male gaze. Three narrative devices are explicated that structure the mockery in the film: stereotypes about depraved and testosterone-obsessed men; portray men as a spectacle for female attention; and the celebration of women’s friendships. The result of the tongue-in-cheek techniques is a strong female gaze that resists and defies patriarchy and opens the film’s text to a feminist reading. As for the TED talk by Stacy Smith, indeed, the situation regarding the role of women in the film industry is disastrous. Thus, nowadays, most films are shot by men and many films still represent the male gaze.

In recent years, social media platforms like Twitter, Instagram, and TikTok have dominated how people consume news and information. Despite this, traditional media such as newspapers, television, and radio still play an important role in today’s world. Although many believe that the rise of social media has made traditional media less relevant, I argue that traditional media continues to serve a crucial function by providing more reliable information and deeper analysis.

One key advantage of traditional media is its commitment to fact-checking and editorial standards. Unlike social media, where anyone can post anything without verification, newspapers and TV channels usually have professional journalists who check the accuracy of information before publishing. For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic, outlets like the BBC and The New York Times provided carefully researched updates, while social media was flooded with rumors and false claims. This shows why people still need traditional media for trustworthy news, especially in times of crisis or uncertainty.

At the same time, social media offers immediacy and widespread reach that traditional media often lacks. News can be shared instantly on platforms like Twitter, where a tweet can go viral within minutes. Traditional media sometimes struggles to keep up with fast-breaking news due to its slower production process. However, social media’s lack of oversight means misinformation can spread quickly, which means traditional media’s role as a reliable source remains important. In that sense, both forms can complement each other rather than completely replace one another.

In addition, traditional media often provides more detailed stories and in-depth analysis compared to short, quick posts on social media. Newspapers can cover topics with more background information and context that might be missing on social platforms focused on brief updates. This allows readers to understand complex issues better, like political events or scientific discoveries. Social media can raise awareness, but it usually doesn’t offer the same depth.

Overall, traditional media still holds value in the age of social media because it ensures quality and depth in information, even though social platforms are faster and more accessible. The two types of media meet different needs, and society benefits when both coexist. It’s not a matter of one replacing the other but more about how they can work together to keep people well-informed.

Conflict Management in the Healthcare Workplace Essay

Conflict management at the workplace is one of the crucial elements related to the organization of work in healthcare facilities. In this regard, McKibben (2017) asserts that conflict is an inevitable part of any human interaction, especially when the collective activity is associated with physical, mental, and ethical complexity found in hospitals. Consequently, if ignored or not handled adequately, the disputes between the colleges at the workplace lead to decreased performance and satisfaction levels of the involved employees (Suifan, Alhyari, & Sweis, 2020). This, in turn, negatively impacts the overall quality of provided patient care. Therefore, it is important to resolve the conflicts as soon as they appear. However, to understand how to manage disputes effectively, one should understand the factors that cause them.

In general, all the antecedents of organizational conflicts may be divided into three groups, namely individual, interpersonal, and organizational. As for the former, Kim et al. (2017) argue that the healthcare professional’s self-esteem, self-focus, emotional intelligence, prevalent responses to conflict, communication styles, and overall worldview determine the frequency and severity of the disputes. In a similar vein, Chang, Chen, and Chen (2017) found that a person’s license level, age, and previous experience of working in other collectives can all affect the behavior during conflict situations. Interpersonal conflicts, on the contrary, are caused by such factors as lack of trust and respect towards a person, power abuse, and ineffective communication (Kim et al., 2017). Finally, organizational conflicts stem from the overall structure and work arrangement. In this respect, such factors as ambiguously defined responsibilities and inadequate hierarchy can cause dissatisfaction and disputes (Kim et al., 2017; McKibben, 2017). Therefore, this type of conflict appears as a result of weak or wrongful management decisions.

I have also participated in several conflicts that can be explained by the factors mentioned above. Firstly, I have a friend who is generally a good person but who is quite self-focused; thus, he often fails to recognize other people’s opinions. Due to that, we usually have to do what he wants, which eventually leads to conflict when I become tired of compromising. Secondly, I have noticed that many conflicts between me and my parents and friends are caused by my inability to control one’s emotions. Finally, once, we had a conflict with my classmates while working on the team project as we failed to discuss the responsibilities of each person before starting.

The rise of remote work has changed many parts of society, especially how cities develop and how urban areas are planned. With more people working from home instead of commuting to offices, the traditional city life is changing rapidly. This shift raises questions about the impact of remote work on urban development and city planning, which is very important as cities are central to economic and social activities. This essay will explore how remote work affects urban structures, commuting patterns, and infrastructure needs, while considering some challenges and opportunities that come with this change.

Urban development has traditionally focused on building dense business districts with office towers and transportation networks that support large numbers of daily commuters. However, as more companies allow employees to work remotely, the need for those dense office spaces might decline. For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic, many major companies in cities like New York and San Francisco reported a significant drop in office occupancy. Some even decided to reduce their physical office space permanently, which affects real estate markets and could lead to changes in how city centers are designed and used. This trend might reduce congestion and pollution but also decrease demand for services that rely on office workers.

On the other hand, this change presents problems for urban planners. Cities have long depended on commuting patterns to organize public transport systems, road networks, and commercial zones. If fewer people use public transport during peak hours due to remote work, cities might face declining revenue and increased maintenance costs for infrastructure that is not used as intensively. Moreover, businesses near city centers, such as cafes and shops, could suffer from reduced foot traffic. For instance, London saw many small businesses struggle during lockdown periods because office workers stopped coming to the city center. Thus, planners need to rethink how to balance these economic shifts while still providing efficient services.

Interestingly, remote work also encourages people to live farther from city centers, often in suburbs or less densely populated areas, because they don’t need to commute every day. This has led to urban sprawl in some regions. For example, suburbs around cities like Austin, Texas, have seen population growth as remote workers seek larger homes and more green space. However, urban sprawl can cause problems of its own: longer travel distances for in-person meetings or social activities, increased car dependence, and challenges in providing utilities and services efficiently. Thus, while remote work offers freedom to workers, it complicates efforts to create sustainable urban environments.

Yet, some cities are adapting by promoting mixed-use development that combines residential, commercial, and recreational spaces closer together, which suits a more flexible working lifestyle. This approach can reduce travel needs for daily activities beyond work, making neighborhoods more lively at different times of day. Cities in Scandinavia, like Stockholm, have experimented successfully with such planning, focusing on walkability and community spaces. Therefore, remote work might push planners toward creating more balanced and human-centered urban designs, rather than areas dominated by office buildings alone.

Remote work also demands better digital infrastructure, such as high-speed internet and reliable telecommunications. Urban planners must now consider technology access as a key component of city development. Without stable internet connections, remote work is impossible for many, especially in lower-income neighborhoods or less developed areas. Thus, cities face the challenge of investing in digital infrastructure alongside traditional physical infrastructure. Areas that fail to improve connectivity risk being left behind economically, which could increase social inequality.

However, some argue that remote work could eventually weaken the cultural and social fabric of cities, which thrive on face-to-face interactions and spontaneous encounters. The vibrancy of urban life depends partly on having people physically present and active in shared spaces. If too many people work from home, city centers might lose their energy, affecting creativity, innovation, and community ties. This presents a subtle but important challenge for urban development that planners must consider, in addition to purely economic or infrastructural factors.

In conclusion, remote work is reshaping urban development and city planning in complex ways. It reduces demand for traditional office spaces and commuting but also creates new challenges, such as urban sprawl and shifts in transportation use. Cities that adapt by encouraging mixed-use areas and investing in digital infrastructure may find new opportunities to thrive. However, the social impacts of decreased physical interaction remain uncertain and require further attention. As remote work continues to evolve, so too must the strategies for creating functional and vibrant urban environments. The future of city planning will likely be less about rigid office districts and more about flexibility and inclusiveness.

A Supporting Human Resource Plan for an Organizational Strategy Essay

The organizational strategy involves the expansion of healthcare institutions in sub-Saharan Africa. Unlike the typical medical services in the field, the institutions would comprise medical records management employees and other statistical professionals. The need for this expansion into the open offices of sub-Sahara Africa can be explained by its rising business and investment opportunities for the particular area through the past decade (Omilola & Sanogo, 2020). High demand for a group of employees to relocate to the chosen destination can then be noted. Considering the political and economic value of each country, it would be best to initially arrange the expansion to the most developed and largest countries of the area. Therefore, the targeted countries include Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa. Moreover, additional countries and locations can be proposed to ensure adequate healthcare development once the business relocation proves successful. The total number of supported relocating employees for all three countries should not exceed thirty per office to allow maximum productivity and financial coverage.

Employees with different levels of experience and expertise will receive varying bonuses and pay changes. However, it is important to establish general policies for all relocating workers. In that way, the move must not compromise the employee’s previous health state and lifestyle (Oyelere & Oyelere, 2021). Commissaries, banking, and currency exchange make up an essential part of the adjustment process and must therefore be provided by the company. The location of the offices would then be close to the leading establishments necessary for domestic purposes. Furthermore, the contrasting climate conditions are to be considered as well, requiring both a medical checkup before the move and setting up urgent-care stations reserved for emergencies. The health of medical professionals and other employees is a particularly principal aspect to plan due to the nature of the business field.

The organization should set an assignment length of one year to gain the necessary data while also building the company’s experience. Research has indicated an increasing number of short-term relocations for problem-solving purposes (Pucik et al., 2017). This statistical finding suggested higher productivity and increased work efficiency in the case of one-year assignments. Consequently, families should consider the disadvantages of traveling in favor of the company’s interests. It is possible that some employees would not choose to relocate with their families for a short period for evident reasons; the move may be inconvenient. Moreover, while a one-year-long assignment is officially recommended, additional work months can be added in specific cases. For instance, in the case of the business goals not being reached or a new project appearing.

As previously mentioned, the decision to relocate along with one’s family would be reviewed by the employees themselves and financed accordingly by the organization. Depending on the structure of each family, including the number and ages of any children, particular arrangements would be necessary. Before organizing the details, each worker must fill out a form indicating the essential information on their moving family members (if any), including any children and their current level of education. One optimal option for incoming school children involves international schools, which would provide an environment of minimal cultural shock and language barriers. One school for all is recommended to ensure an organized arrangement of the employee’s children in the educational field.

Similar to the school grouping, housing the employees would have to be based in its compound of apartments. This decision allows for both safety precautions to be considered and a unified method of financial distribution. Since the planned assignment’s length does not exceed a year, the prospect of the employees selling their housing units is unlikely. Therefore, the suggested plan comprises selecting an apartment block in a safe environment near the school and the workplace. While the organization can compensate for the apartment rent, additional charges, such as water and electricity tariffs, are to be covered by the employees accordingly. The apartments would be similar to each other in terms of furniture and layout, while particular arrangements can be made for larger families. Essentially, communicating the main points and key details of housing plans with the employees before official relocation statements is a vital step to ensure their satisfaction with the level of organization. On the other hand, company managers must be aware of the required conditions to calculate the costs and optimal solutions for the business corporation.

Finally, the organizational strategy must follow the company guidelines while guaranteeing minimal employee stress due to the relocation. Indeed, the main objectives of the business plan must be achieved to improve the healthcare field of several sub-Saharan African countries. In that way, the company’s global impact will also increase in direct proportion to the efficiency of its employees. While funding the workers’ main traveling and family expenses, a safe and shared environment can be offered. Ultimately, the one-year assignment length ensures the mentioned goals are reached while demonstrating the organization’s beneficial mobility.

References

Omilola B., and Sanogo N.A. (2020). Business and investment opportunities in healthcare in Africa. Public Health Open Journal, 5 (1): 11-13. Web.

Oyelere, M., and Oyelere T. (2021). Financial and managerial aspects in human resource management: A practical guide . Emerald Publishing Limited . Web.

Pucik, V., Evans, P., Björkman, I. and Morris, S. (2017). The global challenge: International human resource management (3rd ed.). Chicago, IL: Chicago Business Press.

Business Memo on Foreign Exchange Essay (Article)

On January 1 of this year, our company received information about the spot rate of Malaysian ringgit (MYR) to USD to be 3.13 MYR on April 1; however, on April 1, it became 3.52 MYR. Our team conducted an analysis about the importance of foreign currency exchange for our trade in Malaysia. The main objective of this memo is to demonstrate the results of our evaluation and show that currency exchange is a viable and profitable option for our firm.

The profitability of transactions in international marker is influenced by foreign currency exchange. Since our company has sales contracts with different vendors, we have an obligation to sell a specific number of units that are shipped to Malaysia during the first quarter. Specifically, the firm must sell 4,000 units for 1.25 million MYR within the specified period. Since retailers make payments in their local currency, fluctuation in the exchange rate between MYR and USD may affect our profit. Although we could establish the so-called producer currency pricing to make the customers purchase in USD, it may result in the complete market loss (Monetary and Economic Department [MED], 2018). Therefore, it is essential to maintain international currency exchange because minor alterations MYR/USD rate should not affect its profit.

This memorandum will review three scenarios: adjusting for currency fluctuations, using a fixed rate mentioned in the contract, and avoiding currency exchange by purchasing raw materials in MYR. Firstly, our company could use the spot rate of 3.52 on April 1 to convert its sales revenue in MYR to USD. If the rate was 3.13 MYR per one USD in January, then there was 0.39 points increase on April 1. If 1.25 million MYR is converted to USD in April’s rate, there is a $44,247 loss. Secondly, our firm can lock up January’s rate of 3.13 MYR/USD and thus convert 1.25 million MYR using this value; in this case, the company will have a $44,247 profit. Lastly, the third scenario prevents any currency exchange, avoiding the loss, but it also does not allow a profit.

Although the second case seems to be the most profitable, our firm should consider local retailers’ interests to avoid losing customers. Indeed, currency fluctuation is an inevitable part of the foreign exchange market. Our calculations showed that there is a short-term benefit in converting to USD by a fixed rate. However, there is no actual long-term profitability in reducing domestic currency because the exchange value may go below the ones indicated in a contract (MED, 2018). Therefore, our primary suggestion was to buy raw materials using local currency, which would minimize exchange risks. Nevertheless, after completing calculations for the first two scenarios, we believe that keeping an equal share of USD and MYR will be profitable both in short and long perspectives.

In summary, this memo reviewed the issue of currency fluctuations and the risks of exchange for our firm in the Malaysian market. Considering the available literature and our calculations, we suggest purchasing raw materials using ringgit. At the same time, we recommend having a one-to-one ratio of the U.S. dollar and MYR in this market because the currency conversion brings short-term profit at times when the value of USD rises. If you have any doubts about our proposal, please email us directly. You can also bring your questions to our meeting that will be held in the conference room on February 10, 2022.

Reference

Monetary and Economic Department. (2018). The price, real, and financial effects of exchange rates . BIS Papers , 96, 1-148.

The influence of celebrity culture on young people is a widely discussed topic in contemporary society. Celebrities often become role models, whether intentionally or not, shaping the behavior, attitudes, and values of their fans, especially among the youth. This essay explores the various ways in which celebrity culture affects young people, arguing that while it can inspire and motivate, it also brings challenges related to identity formation and unrealistic expectations.

Celebrity culture, at its core, revolves around the admiration and sometimes obsession with individuals who possess fame and public recognition. Accounts on social media, TV shows, and magazines constantly highlight celebrities’ lifestyles and achievements. Young people, who are in a critical period of developing their self-identity, often look up to these figures in search of guidance or belonging. This phenomenon shows how the media plays a pivotal role in magnifying the reach of celebrities, turning them into powerful role models.

One positive influence of celebrity culture is that it can inspire young people to pursue their dreams. For example, many young athletes are motivated by famous sports stars such as Serena Williams or Cristiano Ronaldo. These celebrities demonstrate the importance of discipline, hard work, and resilience, showing that success is achievable. Moreover, some celebrities use their fame to promote social causes, which can encourage young people to get involved in charity or activism, thus fostering a sense of social responsibility.

However, the impact is not entirely beneficial. The problem arises when young people try to imitate celebrities without critically thinking about the consequences. Many celebrities present a glamorous lifestyle that is often unrealistic or even unhealthy. This can lead to young fans developing distorted ideas about wealth, beauty, and success. For instance, body image issues are common among teenagers influenced by the perfect appearances they see in magazines or Instagram posts. Some cases of eating disorders and low self-esteem can be linked to this kind of pressure.

Another concern is the way celebrity culture sometimes promotes materialism. Young people might believe that acquiring expensive goods or fashion items is a way to gain social status or happiness. This mindset can distract from more important values such as education, kindness, or creativity. Therefore, the emphasis on consumerism and external validation within celebrity culture may negatively shape young people's priorities and decisions.

Moreover, celebrities occasionally behave irresponsibly or set poor examples through their actions. When young people see their idols involved in scandals, substance abuse, or controversial behavior, it can confuse their understanding of right and wrong. Although some may argue that young fans can distinguish between a celebrity’s public image and personal life, it is not always easy during adolescence, a time when critical thinking skills are still developing. Consequently, the glorification of negative behaviors can be harmful.

On the other hand, some argue that celebrity culture is just a reflection of society’s values rather than a cause of problems among young people. Indeed, the media often shows what audiences want to see. If young people admire certain lifestyles or personalities, it might be because these reflect their own desires or frustrations. Yet, this viewpoint does not excuse the responsibility media outlets and celebrities themselves have in promoting positive messages and realistic images.

The case of Billie Eilish, a young singer who openly discusses her struggles with mental health, provides a contrasting example. She has used her platform to raise awareness and encourage young fans to accept themselves and seek help if needed. This shows how celebrity culture can be more than just superficial admiration. It can become a tool for education and support, proving that the impact on young people depends greatly on the kind of celebrities they look up to.

Furthermore, education about media literacy is important to help young people navigate celebrity culture. Teaching them to critically analyze what they see and hear can reduce the risk of blindly following harmful trends or unrealistic standards. Schools and parents can play a role in discussing the differences between appearance and reality, as well as the temporary nature of fame.

It is also worth mentioning that social media platforms amplify the influence of celebrities. Young people spend many hours on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube, where they follow their favorite stars closely. The constant exposure means that celebrities’ messages, behavior, and images can affect their fans more deeply and quickly than before. Despite this, social media can also provide a space for positive interaction and promotion of diverse role models.

In conclusion, celebrity culture has a significant influence on young people, with both positive and negative effects. It can motivate them to achieve goals and engage with social issues, yet it also risks encouraging unrealistic expectations, materialism, and poor behavior. The overall impact depends largely on the type of celebrities admired and the level of critical thinking of the young audience. Approaches such as promoting media literacy and highlighting responsible role models could help minimize the negative effects.

The discussion about celebrity culture is ongoing and complex. It seems unlikely that the influence of famous people on youth will disappear anytime soon, given the media saturation in today’s world. Therefore, understanding and managing this influence is essential for the well-being of future generations. Ultimately, the goal should be to harness the positive aspects of this culture while addressing its challenges thoughtfully.

Streaming services have drastically changed how people consume films and music today. These platforms, like Netflix and Spotify, have made entertainment more accessible than ever, but they have also brought some challenges to the traditional industries. This essay will explore the impacts of streaming services on the film and music sectors, focusing on both positive and negative effects.

Firstly, streaming services provide an easy and affordable way for users to watch movies and listen to music anytime and anywhere. Before streaming, people often had to buy CDs or DVDs, or go to movie theaters. Now, with just a subscription, they can access thousands of titles instantly. This convenience has expanded the audience for many artists and filmmakers who might otherwise remain unknown. For example, Netflix's release of "Roma" helped reach global viewers without relying on traditional cinema distribution.

However, this convenience sometimes hurts art forms that depend on the traditional format. Many independent artists argue that streaming pays them too little compared to album sales or concert tickets. Some famous singers, like Taylor Swift in the past, have criticized Spotify for low royalties. Because revenue from streaming is spread across millions of users and tracks, smaller creators struggle financially. This situation raises concerns about the long-term sustainability of quality content production.

Secondly, streaming platforms have influenced how movies and music are created. Since these services collect a huge amount of user data, they can recommend content based on preferences. While this personalization can improve user experience, it might also limit creativity. Producers may prefer to create formulaic content that fits popular trends rather than experimenting with new ideas. This trend can lead to less diversity in themes and styles, affecting the industry negatively.

On the other hand, streaming has enabled some positive changes in the industry’s structure. For example, Netflix has started producing original films and series, giving new filmmakers more opportunities. Similarly, musicians can use platforms like SoundCloud to launch their careers without needing a record label. This democratic approach benefits underrepresented voices and broadens what audiences can enjoy. Still, these changes also shift power from traditional studios and labels to the streaming companies themselves.

Many people believe that the impact of streaming is mostly for the better because it brings entertainment to more people at lower costs. Yet, it is important to consider who benefits the most from this shift. Streaming giants earn significant profits, but the artists and filmmakers often receive only a small share. This imbalance could harm creativity and diversity in the long run if not addressed, as the industry's business model changes.

In conclusion, streaming services have both opened new doors and created serious challenges for the film and music industry. They offer convenience and wider access but also raise questions about artist compensation and creative freedom. While it is clear that streaming is here to stay, the future depends on finding a balance that supports both consumers and content creators fairly. Hopefully, changes in industry practices can improve this situation over time.
